issues.description: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares a class named 'Course' (problem_statement.md lines 63-74) while the template and solution code define and refer to a class named 'Lecture' (template: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 3; solution: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 3-11). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the lecture/course type) can confuse students about which class they must implement and where the listed attributes and methods belong.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the name consistent: update the UML in problem_statement.md to use the class name 'Lecture' (replace 'class Course' with 'class Lecture') so it matches the exercise text, template, and solution. If 'Course' was intended instead, rename the template and solution classes and all textual references to 'Course' and adjust the UML attributes/methods accordingly. Document the chosen name consistently in the problem statement and code so students are not confused.
